exposure: Infrared monitoring of fetal head skin temperature dynamics
Maternal tolerance to apnea during pregnancy
outcome: Fetal brain arterial blood and oxygen supply
cohort: 35 women at the final stage of physiological delivery and their fetuses.
finding: Infrared local temperature monitoring of the fetus head surface at the final stage of delivery and in the first minutes after birth allows for the assessment of blood and oxygen supply to the fetus brain, timely detection of hypoxia symptoms, and correction of obstetric aid.
mod_finding: In fetuses with low tolerance to delivery factors, immediate artificial induction of contraction or maternal hyperventilation increased fetal head skin temperature and improved outcomes by reducing symptoms of cerebral ischemia.
